checks.trend: Trend (EMA 21/55): passes when the price is above both the 21-day and 55-day averages and the 21 is above the 55. It means buyers currently control the daily trend.
checks.mtf: Timeframes aligned: passes when price is above its 21/55 averages on the 4-hour, daily AND weekly charts. When all three agree, moves tend to last; when they disagree, expect chop.
checks.bollinger: Bollinger: passes on a squeeze with price above the middle band (energy coiled, leaning up) or an upper-band walk (strong trend riding the top band). Touching the lower band alone is not a buy signal.
checks.wyckoff: Wyckoff phase: passes for Spring, Accumulation, Re-accumulation or Markup; fails for Markdown or Distribution. It reads where the big-money cycle is, not the exact entry.
checks.rsi: RSI/momentum: passes when RSI is 40-70 and rising. That is healthy momentum: not exhausted (over 70) and not still falling.
checks.volume: Volume/accumulation: passes when recent volume is above average and more volume trades on up days than down days, i.e. buyers are showing up with size.
checks.floor: Near the floor: passes when price is within 10% of its 7-day, 30-day AND 1-year lows and has not broken support. Cheap and still holding. "Floor at risk" means it just broke support.
checks.smart: Smart money: crypto = whale wallets withdrawing from exchanges or buying on DEXs, plus net long bets of top Hyperliquid traders; stocks = big funds adding in their 13F filings.
checks.insider: Insider/Congress buys: company insiders buying with their own cash (SEC Form 4, code P) or members of Congress disclosing purchases. Filings are delayed, so this shows conviction, not timing.
checks.institutional: Institutional/ETF: passes when a US spot ETF trades or has been filed. ETFs let pensions, IRAs and advisors buy, which adds steady demand.
checks.sentiment: Sentiment: passes when the crowd is not euphoric (Fear & Greed under 75) and futures traders are not paying high funding to stay long (no overheated leverage).
checks.supply: Supply/unlocks: passes when at least 70% of the eventual supply is already circulating, so future unlocks are a smaller threat to price.

phases.Accumulation: Accumulation: after a long fall, price goes sideways in a range while patient buyers absorb selling. It means the decline has paused; it does not mean the rise has started.
phases.Spring: Spring: a quick dip below the bottom of the range that snaps right back inside. It shakes out the last sellers. It counts only if the next test holds above the spring low, ideally on lighter volume.
phases.Re-accumulation: Re-accumulation: a sideways pause after a rise, while the trend averages still point up. It is often a rest stop before the next leg.
phases.Markup: Markup: the phase after accumulation where price trends up. It means the move has started, not that it is about to.
phases.Distribution: Distribution: after a big rise, price goes sideways while early buyers sell to late buyers. It is often a top forming.
phases.Markdown: Markdown: price trending down below falling averages. Don't try to catch it until a range or spring appears.
phases.Range: Range: sideways with no clear prior trend; wait for a break.
phases.Transition: Transition: mixed signals between phases; no clean read.

tags.Consensus: Consensus pick: shows up on 3+ independent lists (Uphold basket, US spot ETF live/filed, listed on Coinbase + Uphold + Binance, top-20% composite score). Many unrelated gatekeepers agree.
tags.Tribal: Tribal: on at most one of those lists. Support mostly comes from its own community; can still run, but fewer outside buyers.
tags.ISO 20022 (community label): ISO 20022 is a banking message standard. "ISO 20022 coins" is a community label, not an official certification; no coin is "approved" by ISO.
tags.Bona fide core: Bona fide core: BTC, ETH, XRP, SOL, LINK, AVAX plus every coin with a live US spot ETF.
